about: Detection cut-offs and Safety bounds for Spec 3 (backend/detection.py load_content). Proposed by the AI / detection lead on 2026-11-15 for the integration lead to approve. Sources checked; see docs/cut-offs-needed.md. Tuned on the four PMData crew replays (ticket 13). Reviewed by the integration lead on 2026-11-15 (Spec 5 ticket 05): linted, AHA links added, glucose and body_temperature bounds added. Still needs qualified medical review.

cutoffs.name: cusum_k
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.2.3 (k = half the shift to detect): https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc323.htm

cutoffs.name: acute_amber
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: 3-sigma limits (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 6.3.2) raised to 4 after tuning on crew replays: 3 gave 0.14 alerts per crew-day, 4 gave 0.11

cutoffs.name: min_anchor_sd
cutoffs.label: team value
cutoffs.source: Tuned on crew replays: a 14-day Anchor gives about 1 bpm spread, too tight for months of real data

cutoffs.name: hr_high
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2025 Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm: heart rate typically >=150/min if tachyarrhythmia. https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms

cutoffs.name: hr_low
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2025 Adult Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm: heart rate typically less than 50 per minute if bradyarrhythmia. https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms

cutoffs.name: sbp_low
cutoffs.label: Earth reference, no space data
cutoffs.source: AHA 2020 Part 3 (Panchal et al.): systolic 90 mmHg is a common hypotension cutoff; definitions vary. https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916

cutoffs.name: return_to_gravity_shift
cutoffs.label: group averages after landing, not limits
cutoffs.source: NASA Apollo AP005, Table 6, first postflight minus preflight (61.6->69.7, 76.4->99.8, 118.8->105.8): https://nlsp.nasa.gov/search/data/details/e1fa5c55-ddfe-5548-91ba-864080319f44?dataType=EXPERIMENTS

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: AHA 2025 Adult Bradycardia and Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithms: https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/algorithms. Not used for resting_heart_rate: AHA notes a low rate can be normal in athletes, and one crew's normal is 49 bpm.

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: AHA 2020 Part 3 (Panchal et al.): systolic 90 mmHg is a common hypotension cutoff. No upper limit sourced. https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, Section 6 (Diabetes Care 2025;48(Suppl 1):S128-S145): Level 1 hypoglycemia is glucose <70 mg/dL; Table 6.2 calls >250 mg/dL level 2 hyperglycemia. These are diabetes-care cut-offs, not values for healthy crew. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11635034/

safety_bounds.label: Earth reference, no space data
safety_bounds.source: CDC ill-traveler definitions (Fever): a measured temperature of 100.4°F [38°C] or greater. No hypothermia limit sourced. https://www.cdc.gov/quarantine/maritime/definitions-signs-symptoms-conditions-ill-travelers.html
